title: Non-EU citizen with Hungarian student card

turns.user: I'm a non-EU citizen attending university in Budapest. Am I automatically excluded from the student pass?
turns.agent:
Not necessarily. Under the 5 November 2026 snapshot, a valid Hungarian higher-education student ID can meet the ID-type requirement without a citizenship restriction. So being a non-EU citizen does not, by itself, automatically exclude you if you have that Hungarian student ID.

If you’re relying instead on an accepted foreign EU/EEA/Swiss or ISIC student ID, the snapshot says EU/EEA/Swiss citizenship and proof of a registered Hungarian address are relevant conditions, along with other requirements such as a valid student ID and qualifying programme type. A non-EU citizen therefore may not meet that route’s stated citizenship condition. The full criteria depend on your ID and programme, so I can’t confirm eligibility from citizenship alone.

Do you have a Hungarian higher-education student ID, or a foreign/ISIC one? Please don’t share ID numbers or documents. For the current rules, see BKK’s monthly student Budapest pass and international-student eligibility update.

This is an independent educational demo, not affiliated with BKK. The snapshot is dated 5 November 2026 and is not live policy verification.
